This covers the woes of abundance, but isn't strictly a Facebook phenomenon, I'd argue sites like tinder are much more harmful in this respect.

I think the bigger issue of Facebook is the highlight reel effect, people naturally share the best parts of their life, to give the best possible impression for social validation. This isn't so bad in itself, but when you multiply this by some 100+ friends the result gives the illusion that your life / relationship is not quite as great as everyone elses. It complete omits that Dave and Mary saved for the best part of a year for that Caribbean trip, or that Harry and Sarah are hiking in silence after their 4th argument today.

It's simply impossible for your life/relationship to outperform the combined selection of 100+ highlight reels in your 'news feed'. In-fact studys prove the contents of news feeds absolutely affects subconscious emotion, feelings of self worth, and depression.
